months.name: January
months.intro: The heart of the dry season: cheap tomatoes, crunchy Jos carrots and the last of the strawberries.

months.name: February
months.intro: Harmattan skies and full stalls. Tomatoes, watermelon and oranges are at their best value.

months.name: March
months.intro: The end of the dry season brings mangoes, early corn and cheap tomatoes. Here’s what to look out for.

months.name: April
months.intro: The first rains arrive. Mangoes peak, sweet corn fills the stalls and leafy greens start to return.

months.name: May
months.intro: Rainy season greens are back: ugu, efo and okra, with the last sweet mangoes of the year.

months.name: June
months.intro: Plenty of leafy greens, okra and garden eggs. Tomatoes get pricier, so buy what you need.

months.name: July
months.intro: Corn is everywhere and greens are cheap. A good month for soups and stews.

months.name: August
months.intro: New yam arrives from the farms, with okra, cucumbers and garden eggs still going strong.

months.name: September
months.intro: New yam season is in full swing, and leafy greens are at their cheapest before the dry months.

months.name: October
months.intro: The rains ease off. Yam, beans and the last of the rainy season greens fill the stalls.

months.name: November
months.intro: Dry season is back: tomatoes and peppers get cheaper, and Jos carrots start to arrive.

months.name: December
months.intro: Festive shopping month: tomatoes, peppers, yam and chicken are in demand, so shop early.

items.name: Tomatoes
items.description: Plum and cherry varieties from Kano, Jos and Ogun.
items.note: Dry season supply keeps prices low

items.name: Mangoes
items.description: Sweet Ogbomoso and Peter mangoes. Best in March.

pick.title: Ogbomoso mangoes
pick.text: Juicy, fibre-light and at their cheapest for the next 3 weeks. Look for fruit that gives a little when pressed.

items.name: Ugu (pumpkin leaves)
items.description: Staple leafy green for soups and stews.
items.note: Rains start in April, supply rising

items.name: Sweet corn
items.description: Roast or boil; buy with husks still green.

items.name: Carrots
items.description: Crunchy Jos carrots, sweetest in the dry season.

items.name: Watermelon
items.description: Heavy for its size means ripe and juicy.

items.name: Strawberries
items.description: Grown on the Jos Plateau. Limited supply.

items.name: Scotch bonnet
items.description: Ata rodo: the heat in every good pepper soup.

items.name: Scent leaf
items.description: Efirin: the fragrant leaf in pepper soup and yam porridge.

items.name: Garden eggs
items.description: Bitter-sweet garden eggs, eaten raw with groundnut paste or in stew.

items.name: Oranges
items.description: Juicy local oranges, great for fresh juice.

items.name: Onions
items.description: Red and white bulbs from the north. Store them somewhere dry and airy.

items.name: Efo tete
items.description: Tender amaranth greens for efo riro.

items.name: Okra
items.description: Pick small, bright pods that snap cleanly.

items.name: Tatashe
items.description: Sweet red pepper that gives stew its colour.

items.name: Cucumber
items.description: Crisp, firm cucumbers for salads and juice.
items.note: Firm and cheap through the rains

items.name: Yam
items.description: New yam arrives from August. Look for firm tubers with no soft spots.

items.name: Plantain
items.description: Green for boiling, ripe yellow and black for dodo.

items.name: Beans
items.description: Oloyin (honey) and brown beans, sold by the mudu.

items.name: Garri
items.description: White and yellow garri, freshly fried and sold by the paint bucket.

items.name: Cassava
items.description: Fresh roots for fufu, garri and abacha.

items.name: Pineapple
items.description: Sweet sugarloaf pineapples. Smell the base to check ripeness.

items.name: Pawpaw
items.description: Soft, sweet pawpaw. Ripe when it gives slightly.

items.name: Eggs
items.description: Free-range and farm eggs, sold by the crate.

items.name: Wara
items.description: Soft Fulani cheese, great fried or in stew.

items.name: Honey
items.description: Raw local honey from Oyo and Kwara hives.

items.name: Local chicken
items.description: Pastured local chicken, firmer and more flavourful.

items.name: Smoked fish
items.description: Catfish, mackerel and bonga smoked over wood.

items.name: Fresh catfish
items.description: Live and fresh catfish from local ponds and the lagoon.
